definitions.explanation: Canceling out a debt, loss, or negative factor. Used both literally (debts) and figuratively (offsetting a disadvantage).

examples.japanese: {借金|しゃっきん}を{帳消|ちょうけ}しにした。
その{一言|ひとこと}で{努力|どりょく}が{帳消|ちょうけ}しになった。
examples.english: That one remark negated all the effort.

examples.japanese: {景色|けしき}の{美|うつく}しさが{長時間|ちょうじかん}の{移動|いどう}の{疲|つか}れを{帳消|ちょうけ}しにしてくれた。
examples.english: The beautiful scenery made up for the fatigue of the long journey.

notes:
USAGE: Almost always used with にする (to write off, to cancel) or になる (to be canceled, to be negated). Very common in figurative use.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {帳消|ちょうけ}しにする: to cancel, to write off, to negate
- {帳消|ちょうけ}しになる: to be canceled out, to be offset
- {借金|しゃっきん}を{帳消|ちょうけ}しにする: to write off a debt

ETYMOLOGY: From {帳|ちょう} (account book) + {消|け}し (erasing) — literally erasing something from the ledger.
